As it happened: GC riders battle it out as race lead changes yet again on Tour de France Femmes stage 8

The 8th stage of the race is the longest at 171.9km in blazing sunshine as the peloton race from Sisteron to Nice with a potential sprint on the Promenade des Anglais.

Live-reports
By Tim Bonville-Ginn
Last updated 8 August 2026

2026-08-08T17:11:25.418Z

And that brings out live report to a close for today. That was another incredible stage at the Tour de France Femmes with a very dramatic day still to come on stage 9 tomorrow. Make sure to join us again for that one. Until then, keep an eye on all the latest reaction, analysis and previews on our home page. Au revoir and have a good rest of your day.

2026-08-08T17:09:40.535Z

Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek) was awarded the most combative rider award after her terrific ride in the breakaway alongside Maeva Squiban (UAE team L'IMAD) who crashed on the descent of the penultimate climb. Adegeest was caught on the final categorised climb with around 9km to go.

2026-08-08T17:07:07.458Z

Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) continues to hold the polka dot jersey. She had won it mathematically before today even started. She now has to focus on finishing and may try for a stage win as well.

2026-08-08T17:02:10.561Z

Canyon-SRAM are still well in the fight for yellow and also continue to hold white as Antonia Niedermaier holds onto her 1'11" lead over Paula Blasi (UAE Team L'IMAD).

2026-08-08T16:59:31.548Z

2026-08-08T16:49:12.475Z

Wiebes extended her lead in the points classification thanks to her taking 17 points in the intermediate sprint.

2026-08-08T16:47:15.360Z

Vollering now leads the Tour de France Femmes by just 8" over Niewiadoma-Phinney with one stage to go. Reusser slips to 1'12" down with Longo-Borghini at over 3 minutes.

2026-08-08T16:45:01.724Z

A big win for Vollering in Nice.

2026-08-08T16:40:45.356Z

Vollering said this after the stage: "In a stage race, you live day by day. So you can be disappointed tonight, but then the next morning you need to put on a new mask and you go again. You try again, you make a plan with the team.

"I think this is proof that if you really believe in something, if you really dream big about something, then it doesn't matter what it needs to take, how much pain it will cost you."

Read more in the link below...

>>> Tour de France Femmes: Demi Vollering seizes maillot jaune with searing late attack

2026-08-08T16:34:13.929Z

The drama continued after the finish in Nice as Niewiadoma-Phinney confronted Gery while the French champion was being interviewed by international media.

2026-08-08T16:17:48.261Z

Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney spoke to various media outlets after the stage calling out FDJ United-Suez's tactics:

"I was annoyed at the beginning of the climb because Gery, on purpose, just blocked me to the barriers where I had to stop pedalling. I feel like, if they want to compete they should compete fair play and not look to block me on the barriers because I feel it is so childish. Honestly, I lost all the respect for them for that."

2026-08-08T16:12:11.604Z

2026-08-08T16:06:32.112Z

Le Court leads in the chase group ahead of Kopecky and the rest.

2026-08-08T16:06:13.277Z

The clock starts ticking... And Vollering is the new yellow jersey of the Tour de France Femmes with one day to go with a handful of seconds in it!

2026-08-08T16:05:25.272Z

Demi Vollering wins stage 8 of the Tour de France Femmes 2026!

2026-08-08T16:05:08.952Z

500 metres to go. Yellow is changing hands.

2026-08-08T16:04:46.023Z

Flamme Rouge!

The final 1000 metres of racing today for Vollering. 17" back to Niewiadoma-Phinney and Longo-Borghini.

2026-08-08T16:03:58.972Z

Vollering is virtual leader once again.

2026-08-08T16:03:43.135Z

2km to go. The gap continues to grow and Niewiadoma-Phinney can see her yellow jersey disappear up the road.

2026-08-08T16:02:46.320Z

Longo-Borghini is riding for time as she has a lot of it to close on Reusser in the chase for the podium.

2026-08-08T16:02:07.794Z

Vollering turns left onto the Promenade des Anglais. Just 7" splits her and the chase of Longo-Borghini and Niewiadoma-Phinney. This is tight!

2026-08-08T16:01:30.550Z

4km to go and the gap closes to 9". Some incredible power being put down by Longo-Borghini in this chase. Can she save this yellow jersey for Niewiadoma-Phinney?

2026-08-08T16:00:51.337Z

5km to go

Vollering has taken 22" already and is victual yellow jersey. Niewiadoma-Phinney and Longo-Borghini have so much to close here. Vollering only needs 16" to take yellow from Niewiadoma-Phinney.

2026-08-08T15:59:49.527Z

Attack!

Demi Vollering (FST)

She has the gap! Niewiadoma-Phinney and Longo-Borghini can not follow the European champion. She is flying down this rapid descent but she has two superb descenders chasing her.

2026-08-08T15:59:02.984Z

Vollering goes again but Niewiadoma-Phinney finds her power and makes it to Vollering.

2026-08-08T15:58:41.047Z

The yellow jersey is struggling to get onto the wheel as the Italian champion makes it to Vollering.

2026-08-08T15:58:18.640Z

Attack!

Demi Vollering (FST)

She goes clear with Longo-Borghini and Niewiadoma-Phinney bridging the gap.

2026-08-08T15:57:38.196Z

It is now a gradual descent where you need to stay on the pedals before they turn onto an absolute wall of just 700 metres at 17%.

2026-08-08T15:57:06.456Z

QOM (Côte de la Ginestière)

1. Gery (FST) 2pts
2. Vollering (FST) 1pt

2026-08-08T15:56:38.930Z

Gery leads ahead of Vollering, Niewiadoma-Phinney, Longo-Borghini, Le Court, Blasi, Kerbaol, Reusser, De Vriees, Niedermaier, Włodarczyk and a couple of others holding on as they crest the climb.

2026-08-08T15:55:19.846Z

Berthet swings off the front and Celia Gery takes over for Vollering,

2026-08-08T15:55:02.229Z

Wiebes dropped! They still have Kopecky in the lead group, though.

2026-08-08T15:54:07.491Z

Adegeest caught by the Berthet led peloton.

2026-08-08T15:53:53.697Z

Koch swings off with Berthet taking over. The white jersey of Antonia Niedermaier (Canyon-SRAM) starting to struggle.

2026-08-08T15:52:55.563Z

Koch turning herself inside out on this climb with Juliette Berthet on her wheel with Vollering. Then it is all the other big GC riders including the yellow jersey. But, significantly, also Wiebes.

2026-08-08T15:52:03.608Z

Onto the final categorised climb of the Côte de la Ginestière. 2.5km at 4.4%. FDJ United-SUEZ leads with Franziska Koch leading the way with Vollering in third wheel.

2026-08-08T15:50:57.812Z

10km to go

Loes Adegeest has 43" on the peloton and is giving her all. But, the climbing to come is going to be hard to hold on over the top.

2026-08-08T15:48:44.072Z

The peloton spread across the road with multiple teams leading the way in colour order.

2026-08-08T15:48:04.400Z

Squiban caught by the peloton with 12km to go. Visma-Lease a Bike move up to the front likely for Marianna Vos.

2026-08-08T15:47:11.467Z

Squiban still hasn't been caught by the peloton but Adegeest is still out front and pushing hard.

2026-08-08T15:45:57.005Z

Squiban screaming with pain as she was being treated by the medic bike. We didn't need to see that.

2026-08-08T15:45:26.940Z

Crash

Usoa Ostolaza (LAB)

The Spanish rider goes down in the peloton a couple of corners after the one Squiban came down.

2026-08-08T15:44:48.228Z

Squiban got back riding and was very quick to her feet to get going again. However, she has now settled down and she can't hold the handlebars and looks in a lot of pain.

2026-08-08T15:43:36.640Z

Crash!

Maeva Squiban (UAD)

She slid out on the descent after taking a few too many risks. She looks very panicked. Adegeest now solo out front.

2026-08-08T15:42:22.391Z

FDJ United-SUEZ and Human Powered Health move up to the front and push Canyon-SRAm out.

2026-08-08T15:41:34.159Z

QOM (Côte de Colomars)

1. Squiban (UAD) 2pts
2. Adegeest (LTK) 1pt

2026-08-08T15:40:57.782Z

Onto the Côte de Colomars they go. The cat 4 climb is 1.4km long with an average gradient of 5.4% as Zoe Backstedt comes to the front with her leader Niewiadoma-Phinney on her wheel.

2026-08-08T15:38:41.010Z

Movistar and EF Education-Oatly both come to the front now to join the pace setting. The latter surely looking at Cedrine Kerbaol for a descent attack into Nice.

2026-08-08T15:37:54.864Z

Niewiadoma-Phinney has had a very quiet day in the peloton wearing yellow. Nowhere near the front for the whole day.

2026-08-08T15:36:24.494Z

20km to go

The gap drops under 2 minutes for the first time in a long time as the climbs begin very soon.

2026-08-08T15:30:52.108Z

Lore De Schepper (AGS) also now dropped from the peloton after working hard for Kim Le Court.

2026-08-08T15:29:58.883Z

Marion Bunel (TVL) has found herself out of the back due to the pace. She continues to struggle at this race.

2026-08-08T15:29:31.731Z

At this rate, the riders out front have a leeway of 30" on the current time loss rate. However, they have two cat 4 climbs and a 400 metre kicker of 17% where the peloton will definitely claim those spare 30", so this should be going the way of the peloton in Nice.

2026-08-08T15:27:39.503Z

The peloton is very strung out as the road tightens with nerves going up. Another 5km ridden and another 30" gone from the gap. 25km to go and the gap is 2'58".

2026-08-08T15:25:54.412Z

Crash!

Nikola Noskova (COF)
Nadia Gontova (LIV)
Alice Coutinho (MMM)
Marine Allione (MMM)

Second crash today for Coutinho.

2026-08-08T15:22:07.671Z

30km to go

Multiple teams now working hard on the front with SD Worx-Protime also joining in. Squiban and Adegeest now have 3'35" with 30km to go.

2026-08-08T15:21:16.596Z

This was a few minutes ago. The gap is now much lower.

2026-08-08T15:18:08.480Z

Adegeest and Squiban are losing 30" every 5km. With that calculation, it will be about 10" roughly by the finish, so that is very touch and go.

2026-08-08T15:15:46.491Z

The pace is on in the peloton.

2026-08-08T15:14:40.305Z

Gap seems to be stabilised around 4'22" between the leader and the peloton.

2026-08-08T15:07:31.357Z

40km to go

Loes Adegeest and Maeva Squiban hold 4'33" over the peloton. This is going to be tight in the final. About 20km to the penultimate climb.

2026-08-08T15:02:57.764Z

Gap continuing to drop and is at 4'39" to Squiban and Adegeest with the peloton working very hard.

2026-08-08T15:02:02.892Z

Consonni returns to the back of the peloton.

2026-08-08T14:59:44.920Z

Bike change

Chiara Consonni (Canyon-SRAM)

She had a puncture.

2026-08-08T14:57:34.453Z

50km to go

The gap drops to under five minutes for the first time in a very long time. The peloton are coming back into the game as the leading duo tire.

2026-08-08T14:52:54.340Z

In the space of 5km the gap has dropped by about 30". This is starting to look like it may be starting to be more in favour of the peloton.

2026-08-08T14:50:36.152Z

The riders have been cycling through a beautiful part of France.

2026-08-08T14:47:52.092Z

The gap is starting to come down a bit more now. 5'24" is the gap, but it isn't coming down quickly at all.

2026-08-08T14:44:56.743Z

The top 3 in the points classification after that:

1. Wiebes (SDW) 164pts
2. Kopecky (SDW) 98pts
3. Le Court (AGS) 89pts

2026-08-08T14:44:01.302Z

Intermediate sprint (Puget-Théniers)

1. Loes Adegeest (Lidl-Trek) 25pts
2. Maëva Squiban (UAE Team L’IMAD) 20pts
3. Lorena Wiebes (SD Worx-Protime) 17pts
4. Mischa Bredewold (SD Worx-Protime) 15pts
5. Lotte Kopecky (SD Worx-Protime) 13pts
6. Ruby Roseman-Gannon (Liv-AlUla-Jayco) 11pts
7. Elena Cecchini (SD Worx-Protime) 10pts
8. Évita Muzic (FDJ United-Suez) 9pts
9. Justine Ghekiere (AG Insurance-Soudal) 8pts
10. Lore de Schepper (AG Insurance-Soudal) 7pts
11. Letizia Borghesi (AG Insurance-Soudal) 6pts
12. Mackenzie Coupland (Liv-AlUla-Jayco) 5pts
13. Nadia Gontova (Liv-AlUla-Jayco) 4pts
14. Juliette Berthet (FDJ United-Suez) 3pts
15. Thalita de Jong (Human Powered Health) 2pts

2026-08-08T14:41:30.481Z

Meanwhile, Wiebes coasts across the intermediate sprint and takes 17 points.

2026-08-08T14:40:55.648Z

Squiban was very stressed for some time as the team car was taking a very long time to get up to her. Her car are now trying to calm the French rider down and focus on the race as they have a big chance to take a stage.

2026-08-08T14:36:44.321Z

UAE Team L'IMAD faced a lot of criticism at the start of the race as Paula Blasi focuses on supporting Elisa Long-Borghini instead of going for GC herself after an amazing season so far. But now, Longo-Borghini, Blasi and Dominika Włodarczyk are all in the top 10 in 4th, 7th and 8th while also having Squiban in the break today, it is going very well for them...

>>> 'It just became a massive ball of stress' – Paula Blasi and UAE Team L'IMAD united on Mont Ventoux after challenging week at Tour de France Femmes

2026-08-08T14:34:04.679Z

Adegeest crossed the line at the intermediate sprint first ahead of Squiban with just under six minutes back to the peloton.

2026-08-08T14:26:50.864Z

70km to go

AG Insurane-Soudal and Liv-AlUla-Jayco bring up more riders to work on the front along with a couple from FDJ United-SUEZ with the gap at 6'16".

2026-08-08T14:24:28.516Z

The gap grows further to 6'20" now.

2026-08-08T14:19:45.525Z

Squiban is now going to get her team car as they pass the peloton.

2026-08-08T14:19:22.691Z

The peloton aren't really closing the gap at the moment.

2026-08-08T14:16:36.302Z

Squiban taking bidons from the Lidl-Trek and Shimano Neutral Service car as her team car isn't up there with her, interestingly.

2026-08-08T14:13:30.994Z

80km to go

The break of Squiban and Adegeest have extended their gap to 6'07" on the peloton with 15km to go until the intermediate sprint.

2026-08-08T14:11:40.286Z

The riders have crossed the halfway point.

2026-08-08T14:10:20.316Z

The peloton are upping the pace but they are not closing the gap with much speed. It is holding at 5'50" at the moment with 84km to go.

2026-08-08T14:04:43.251Z

90km to go

The gap drops to 5'44" thanks to Justine Ghekiere of AG Insurance-Soudal.

2026-08-08T14:01:49.549Z

It is now a long descent pretty much all the way to the penultimate climb with around 18km to go.

2026-08-08T14:00:43.339Z

AG Insurance-Soudal and FDJ United-SUEZ rejoin the front of the peloton alongside Liv-AlUla-Jayco with 94km to go. 5'57" up to the break.

2026-08-08T13:59:50.817Z

QOM (Col de Toutes Aures)

1. Squiban (UAD) 2pts
2. Adegeest (LTK) 1pt

2026-08-08T13:57:58.214Z

The break are 500 metres from the top of the Col de Toutes Aures.

2026-08-08T13:56:36.948Z

Liv-AlUla-Jayco doing the work at the front of the peloton with one rider. However, they have Lidl-Trek sat behind her, basically all the riders from that team defending Adegeest's lead out front.

2026-08-08T13:54:20.176Z

Before the break even got away it was certain that Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) had won the polka-dot jersey. She needs to finish both stages in the time cut, but she can now focus on stage wins.

2026-08-08T13:49:08.663Z

Coston caught by the peloton. 6'00" gap up to Adegeest and Squiban.

2026-08-08T13:46:16.691Z

100km to go

The peloton change the pace and the gap drops by about 15" very quickly. Coston now only has 15" gap on the bunch.

2026-08-08T13:44:31.305Z

Nadia Gontova (Liv-AlUla-Jayco) and Justine Ghekiere (AG Insurance-Soudal) lead the peloton.

2026-08-08T13:43:24.078Z

The gap to the peloton goes over six minutes.

2026-08-08T13:38:52.285Z

Now about 10km to the top of the next climb, the Col de Toutes Aures. Cat 4, 6.4km long, 3.1% average.

2026-08-08T13:35:13.688Z

110km to go

Adegeest and Squiban have 5'00" on Coston with the peloton just 45" behind.

2026-08-08T13:34:38.198Z

QOM (Col des Robines)

1. Adegeest (LTK) 2pts

2026-08-08T13:24:53.950Z

2026-08-08T13:23:49.558Z

2026-08-08T13:19:05.181Z

2026-08-08T13:14:09.396Z

Squiban and Adegeest have 2'35" over Coston and 3'05" over the peloton. The average speed is up at 43.5kph so far.

2026-08-08T13:12:38.762Z

It has been very chaotic in the peloton with several riders trying to get up the road. Multiple teams have tried many times but none are getting a gap.

2026-08-08T13:09:39.340Z

2026-08-08T13:06:45.967Z

Morgane Coston (Ma Petite Entreprise)

She is trying to bridge to Squiban and Adegeest. She currently is 1'45" back and just 15" ahead of the peloton.

2026-08-08T13:02:15.256Z

2026-08-08T12:51:44.167Z

2026-08-08T12:46:32.572Z

2026-08-08T12:04:35.069Z

To get to Nice from Sisteron the organisers could have chosen a brutal day in the Maritime Alps. But, after the finish on Mont Ventoux yesterday and the laps around Col d'Eze tomorrow, they have gone with this 'flatter' terrain to give some potential to recover a bit on the bike. That said, with the neutral the riders are going 182km.

2026-08-08T11:32:51.305Z

Breaking news!

Pauline Ferrand-Prévot (Visma-Lease a Bike) will not start today's stage after feeling unwell over night. The defending champion has had a Tour to forget.

2026-08-08T11:20:21.360Z

Unfortunately, one rider didn't make the time cut on Mont Ventoux yesterday. Charlotte Kool (Alpecin-Premier Tech) missed it and is out of the race.

>>> Charlotte Kool leaves the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift after finishing outside the time limit on the punishing stage to Mont Ventoux

2026-08-08T11:17:19.396Z

Yesterday was a very special day for Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney as the Canyon-SRAM rider moved into yellow for the first time since she was crowned overall winner in 2024. She has two days to go but they aren't straightforward in the slightest!

>>> 'A payback for all the second and third places' – Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney pulls out all the stops to move within reach of second Tour de France Femmes title

2026-08-08T11:11:07.761Z

Teams have been completing sign on and rider presentation in Sisteron before the start that will come in roughly half an hours time. 13:40 local time is when the neutral start is scheduled.

2026-08-08T11:06:49.434Z

Starting in Sisteron the route gradually climbs almost constantly for the first 77km with the rest of the day almost entirely being downhill before the final 20km where the climbs come before a mad dash to the line in Nice.

2026-08-08T11:04:20.397Z

Today is the longest stage of the race with a tough route that takes on four category four climbs along the route with two of them coming in the final 20km. That said, it is expected to be a sprint with Lorena Wiebes (SD Worx-Protime) saying her team are going all in for her...
